color.note: Semantic names only. Nothing in the app references a hex value or a primitive ramp; if a colour is needed that no token names, the token is missing. Light is authored first, dark is authored beside it — neither is a tint of the other.

tokens.name: surface-canvas
tokens.usage: The window ground behind every pane. Sidebar, gutters and the space between panes.

tokens.name: surface-base
tokens.usage: The reading surface of a pane: run tree, timeline, forms, tables. Default ground for ink-primary, ink-secondary and ink-tertiary.

tokens.name: surface-raised
tokens.usage: Things that float: command palette, popovers, menus, the gate card, dialogs. Pair with shadow-popover, never with a heavier border.

tokens.name: surface-sunken
tokens.usage: Wells that hold machine text: the agent output pane, YAML source view, artifact body, diff gutters.

tokens.name: surface-overlay
tokens.usage: Scrim behind a modal dialog or the command palette. Never carries text.

tokens.name: surface-hover
tokens.usage: Row and control hover. Layered over whatever ground is beneath, so it works on base, raised and sunken alike.

tokens.name: surface-active
tokens.usage: Pressed state for rows and controls, and the ground of an open disclosure header.

tokens.name: surface-selected
tokens.usage: The selected run tree row, selected timeline entry, selected grid cell. Keyboard selection uses this plus border-focus, never this alone.

tokens.name: border-hairline
tokens.usage: Purely decorative separation: row rules, pane splits, table lines. Structure in this system is drawn with hairlines instead of shadows. Exempt from the 3:1 floor because removing it never hides a control — anything that must be seen to be used takes border-default.

tokens.name: border-control
tokens.usage: The boundary that identifies an interactive control or a graph node: inputs, buttons, selects, checkboxes, workflow and dependency nodes. Holds 3:1 on surface-canvas, surface-base, surface-raised and surface-sunken in both themes.

tokens.name: border-strong
tokens.usage: Emphasis edge: hovered control, the frame of an expanded step, a graph node on the executed path. 5:1 or better on every pane ground in both themes.

tokens.name: border-focus
tokens.usage: The 2px focus ring, drawn outside the control with a 1px offset. At least 3:1 on canvas, base, raised, sunken and every status tint in both themes.

tokens.name: ink-primary
tokens.usage: Body copy, row labels, headings, values. On surface-canvas, surface-base, surface-raised, surface-sunken and every status tint.

tokens.name: ink-secondary
tokens.usage: Supporting text that still must be read: timestamps, durations, field help, secondary columns. On surface-base and surface-raised.

tokens.name: ink-tertiary
tokens.usage: Lowest-emphasis text that is still text: placeholder, disabled label, gutter line numbers, breadcrumb separators. Holds 4.5:1 on surface-canvas, surface-base, surface-raised and surface-sunken in both themes.

tokens.name: ink-inverse
tokens.usage: Text and icons on a filled ink-primary ground, such as a keyboard-shortcut badge in the command palette.

tokens.name: accent
tokens.usage: Interactive intent and nothing else: links, primary button fill, active nav item, selection edge, focus. Never used to mean a run state. On surface-base and surface-raised.

tokens.name: accent-hover
tokens.usage: Hover and press for anything painted with accent.

tokens.name: accent-subtle
tokens.usage: Ground of the active sidebar item and of an accent-toned inline hint. Carries ink-primary or accent.

tokens.name: on-accent
tokens.usage: Text and icons on an accent fill. Light theme puts near-white on deep teal; dark theme puts near-black on bright teal — do not hardcode white.

tokens.name: status-running
tokens.usage: The running state: label text, chip text, icon, the left rail of a running row, an active graph edge in a run overlay. On surface-base and on status-running-bg.

tokens.name: status-running-bg
tokens.usage: Chip and rail tint behind status-running text.

tokens.name: status-waiting
tokens.usage: Waiting on a human — a gate or a permission ask. The loudest status in the system and the only one allowed in the title bar and sidebar counts. On surface-base and on status-waiting-bg.

tokens.name: status-waiting-bg
tokens.usage: Chip, rail and attention-inbox row tint behind status-waiting text.

tokens.name: status-succeeded
tokens.usage: Succeeded and completed. Used at chip scale only — success is the expected outcome and never fills a row. On surface-base and on status-succeeded-bg.

tokens.name: status-succeeded-bg
tokens.usage: Chip tint behind status-succeeded text.

tokens.name: status-failed
tokens.usage: Failed steps, failed runs, failed dependencies, handshake errors. On surface-base and on status-failed-bg.

tokens.name: status-failed-bg
tokens.usage: Chip and rail tint behind status-failed text.

tokens.name: status-cancelled
tokens.usage: Cancelled by a person. Neutral by design: a cancel is not a fault. Always drawn with the slashed-circle glyph. On surface-base and on status-cancelled-bg.

tokens.name: status-cancelled-bg
tokens.usage: Chip tint behind status-cancelled text.

tokens.name: status-blocked
tokens.usage: Blocked by an open dependency. Distinct from failed because nothing went wrong and from waiting because no person is being asked. On surface-base and on status-blocked-bg.

tokens.name: status-blocked-bg
tokens.usage: Chip tint behind status-blocked text.

tokens.name: status-held
tokens.usage: Held by the scheduler: ready to run but restrained by risk exposure or appetite. On surface-base and on status-held-bg.

tokens.name: status-held-bg
tokens.usage: Chip tint behind status-held text.

tokens.name: status-stale
tokens.usage: Data older than the live connection: last-known values while reconnecting or disconnected. Neutral like cancelled — tell them apart by the clock glyph and the dashed border, never by hue. On surface-base and on status-stale-bg.

tokens.name: status-stale-bg
tokens.usage: Chip tint behind status-stale text, and the ground of a stale-data banner.

tokens.name: diff-add-bg
tokens.usage: Added lines in an artifact version diff. Paired with a leading plus sign, never colour alone.

tokens.name: diff-remove-bg
tokens.usage: Removed lines in an artifact version diff. Paired with a leading minus sign.

tokens.name: graph-edge
tokens.usage: Workflow and dependency graph edges that a run did not traverse, and the run-tree indent guides. Holds 3:1 on surface-canvas, surface-base and surface-raised — graph structure is meaningful non-text content, so it is never drawn at hairline strength.

tokens.name: graph-edge-active
tokens.usage: Edges on the path a run actually took, and a satisfied dependency edge. Carries an arrowhead as well as the colour.

tokens.name: risk-low
tokens.usage: Risk matrix cell ground for the core level low: a score below the plan's thresholds.medium (1–4 on the default 5×5). Carries ink-primary.

tokens.name: risk-moderate
tokens.usage: Risk matrix cell ground for the core level medium: from thresholds.medium up to thresholds.high (5–9 on the default 5×5). Carries ink-primary.

tokens.name: risk-high
tokens.usage: Risk matrix cell ground for the core level high: from thresholds.high up to thresholds.critical (10–15 on the default 5×5). Carries ink-primary.

tokens.name: risk-severe
tokens.usage: Risk matrix cell ground for the core level critical: from the plan's thresholds.critical up (16–25 on the default 5×5). Carries ink-primary and a hatched overlay so the band survives greyscale.

type.note: Two tracks. Sans carries the interface; mono carries everything ORCA produced — ids, step names, node names, paths, agent output, artifact bodies. A reader should be able to tell at a glance whether a string came from a person or from the system.
type.fontsNote: Bundled with the app as woff2, never fetched: an Electron app that needs a CDN to render its own text is broken offline. The files live in packages/design/fonts and are subsets — tools/font-build/build-fonts.js produces them from the upstream releases and verifies the coverage. `file` is relative to css/tokens.css, which is where the generated @font-face rules land.
type.familiesNote: The two Noto faces come first on purpose. Plex ships none of the status glyphs (◐ ◆ ✕ ⊘ ▣ ⏸ ◷ ●), so without them every glyph falls through to whatever the OS has — a different face per platform, at chip scale, beside the word. Both are subset to exactly the glyphs ORCA renders and contain no Latin, not even a space, so they cannot touch text; the build script enforces that. Plex follows, then the per-OS fallbacks, so Linux, macOS and Windows each land on a reasonable face if a file fails to load; no OS's system font is assumed.

families.sans: "Noto Sans Symbols 2", "Noto Sans Math", "IBM Plex Sans", "Segoe UI", Ubuntu, Cantarell, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif
families.mono: "Noto Sans Symbols 2", "Noto Sans Math", "IBM Plex Mono", ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, "DejaVu Sans Mono", monospace

styles.name: display
styles.usage: The one large heading on an empty state or a first-run screen. Not used in the shell.

styles.name: title
styles.usage: Screen title in the object header: a request summary, a plan name, a config file name.

styles.name: heading
styles.usage: Pane headers, section headers in a config form, card titles.

styles.name: body
styles.usage: Default interface text: row labels, prose, field values, menu items.

styles.name: body-strong
styles.usage: The one emphasised thing in a row — a work item title, a gate question, the agent name in a tool call.

styles.name: label
styles.usage: Secondary row text, table cells, timestamps, form labels, button text.

styles.name: label-strong
styles.usage: Column headers, chip text, active tab, the label of a focused field.

styles.name: caption
styles.usage: Field help, counts, relative times, the second line of a two-line row.

styles.name: eyebrow
styles.usage: Uppercase group headers in the sidebar and the command palette. Sentence content is never set in this style.

styles.name: mono-body
styles.usage: Artifact bodies, YAML source, step and node names, file paths, expressions.

styles.name: mono-strong
styles.usage: The name of the thing itself in a row: a workflow node name, a tool name, a changed key in a diff.

styles.name: mono-log
styles.usage: Streamed agent output and tool-call payloads. Line height is tight enough that a screen of log is worth scrolling and loose enough to read.

styles.name: mono-id
styles.usage: Run ids, event ids, commit shas, artifact versions. Tracked out slightly so a truncated id can still be compared by eye.

spacing.note: A 4px grid. Everything in the shell lands on it, and the half rungs — space-0-5, space-1-5, space-2-5 — are the three places it does not. A gap between two things is always a whole step; a half rung is inline padding inside a control, where the box is set by a height the grid does not divide and the padding has to balance it optically (#244). Half rungs stop at 10px: above that the grid is never the wrong answer.

tokens.name: space-0-5
tokens.usage: Gap between a status glyph and its label; chip inner leading.

tokens.name: space-1
tokens.usage: Tightest gap: icon to text, chip to chip.

tokens.name: space-1-5
tokens.usage: Inline padding of a chip — space-1 crowds the glyph against the border and space-2 makes an 18px chip read as a button. Also the overhang of a flag pinned half off a graph node's corner.

tokens.name: space-2
tokens.usage: Inline gap inside a row, cell padding in a compact table, gap between chips.

tokens.name: space-2-5
tokens.usage: Inline padding of a button and of a segment in a segmented control: the rung between space-2 and space-3 that balances control-md's 28px box.

tokens.name: space-3
tokens.usage: Row horizontal padding, gap between a label and its control, one run-tree indent step.

tokens.name: space-4
tokens.usage: Pane padding, card padding, gap between form fields.

tokens.name: space-5
tokens.usage: Gap between a card's header and its body.

tokens.name: space-6
tokens.usage: Gap between sections within a pane; command palette padding.

tokens.name: space-8
tokens.usage: Gap between major blocks on a screen; empty-state inset.

tokens.name: space-12
tokens.usage: Top and bottom inset of a centred empty or error state.

tokens.name: space-16
tokens.usage: The largest inset, used once per screen at most.

radius.note: Tight. A paper-and-ink system reads as drawn, not moulded; nothing in the shell is rounder than 10px and nothing is a pill except a status dot.

tokens.name: radius-none
tokens.usage: Table cells, pane edges, the risk matrix, full-bleed rows.

tokens.name: radius-xs
tokens.usage: Chips, badges, keyboard-shortcut keys, inline code.

tokens.name: radius-sm
tokens.usage: Buttons, inputs, selects, tree rows when selected.

tokens.name: radius-md
tokens.usage: Cards, graph nodes, the expanded step frame, tool-call rows.

tokens.name: radius-lg
tokens.usage: Floating surfaces: command palette, dialogs, popovers.

tokens.name: radius-full
tokens.usage: Status dots and the run progress meter cap only.

shadow.note: Elevation is scarce. Structure comes from hairlines; shadow means only 'this floats above the window' and appears on at most one element at a time.

tokens.name: shadow-none
tokens.usage: The default for every pane, card, row and graph node.

tokens.name: shadow-popover
tokens.usage: Menus, popovers, the schedule explanation bubble, autocomplete.

tokens.name: shadow-modal
tokens.usage: Command palette and dialogs, over surface-overlay.

tokens.name: shadow-sticky
tokens.usage: A sticky header that currently has content scrolled beneath it — applied only while scrolled, so the seam appears when it means something.

size.note: Three row heights carry the whole app. Comfortable is the default; compact is the density toggle, persisted per surface; the log line is a row too, so a stream of agent output virtualises on the same substrate as a tree of steps. A surface binds one of them to --row-h and nothing restates it. Six prefixes divide the rest, and the divisions are the point (#244). control-* is a pointer target and nothing else: hit-min (24px) is the smallest comfortable one, and the two rungs #244 added extend the family without loosening that — control-xs is a segment inside a group where the group is the target, and control-sm-5 is the half rung between sm and md, named the way spacing names space-0-5. badge-* is the family that is deliberately not control-*: a chip, a key cap, a schedule badge and a reference are marks that say something, never things you click, so their heights sit below hit-min on purpose and a control must never borrow one. bar-* is a band of chrome across a pane or a window — a height, but not a height you click either. mark-* is decorative geometry; the scale has two rungs, and where a mark's size is dictated by the thing it sits on rather than by the scale it is named for that thing. col-* is a fixed track sized to what it holds, the way col-time is sized to a timestamp. Everything else is one named box.

tokens.name: row-comfortable
tokens.usage: Default height of a run tree row, timeline entry, table row, list item.

tokens.name: row-compact
tokens.usage: The same rows under the density toggle, for trees of hundreds of steps.

tokens.name: row-log
tokens.usage: One line of streamed agent output, so the log pane can bind --row-h to it and the list substrate reads it back unchanged. Derived from mono-log's line height rather than restating it: the type scale decides how tall a line of log is, and a row of log is a line.

tokens.name: hit-min
tokens.usage: The smallest comfortable pointer target. A mark that is also a control — a minimap tick — draws at its mark size and takes its target from here.

tokens.name: mark-sm
tokens.usage: A decorative mark's thickness: a minimap tick, a meter track, and the sliver of the sheet stacked behind a parallel node. Not a control and not a border, so neither the control family nor the stroke family names it.

tokens.name: mark-md
tokens.usage: A decorative mark that has to read at a glance rather than as a line: the status dot, and the width of the caret at the end of streaming output. Still not a control — a dot that can be clicked takes hit-min for its target.

tokens.name: mark-port
tokens.usage: A connection port on a graph node's edge. Sized to the edge it terminates rather than to the mark scale, so it is named for what it is.

tokens.name: mark-skeleton
tokens.usage: The thickness of a skeleton line while a surface loads. Reads as a line of text at rest without pretending to be one.

tokens.name: mark-swatch
tokens.usage: The length of the stroke sample in a graph legend: enough of an edge to show whether it is solid, dashed or dotted.

tokens.name: hatch-period
tokens.usage: The repeat of the 45° hatch over the risk matrix's severe band, whose stripe is one stroke-hairline. Rule 4 makes this geometry rather than decoration: the top band is hatched so severity is not carried by colour alone, and a hatch too fine to see would break that.

tokens.name: bar-status
tokens.usage: The status bar across the bottom of the window. The shortest bar, because it carries one line of caption and no control.

tokens.name: bar-pane
tokens.usage: A pane's header bar: its title, and the controls that act on that pane.

tokens.name: bar-title
tokens.usage: The window title bar, the one bar the OS also has an opinion about — see the titlebar-inset-* tokens.

tokens.name: bar-object
tokens.usage: The object header above a primary pane: the breadcrumb, the object's name and its actions. The tallest bar, because it is the one a person reads to know where they are.

tokens.name: badge-sm
tokens.usage: A status chip, the square a glyph-only chip draws, and a keyboard key cap. A mark that carries a word, not a pointer target — it sits below hit-min deliberately.

tokens.name: badge-md
tokens.usage: A schedule badge, a reference chip, the title bar's waiting count, the pinned marker. The rung above badge-sm, for a mark that stands alone rather than inside a row of text.

tokens.name: col-time
tokens.usage: The event timeline's time column, sized to 00:00:00 in mono-id.

tokens.name: col-lineno
tokens.usage: The log pane's line-number gutter, sized to five digits in mono-log.

tokens.name: col-label
tokens.usage: The label column of a config form, sized to a setting's name in label-strong without wrapping it.

tokens.name: col-label-narrow
tokens.usage: The same label column in the inspector, where the pane is a third of the width. One column at two widths, not two columns.

tokens.name: col-node-kind
tokens.usage: The node-kind column in a node list, sized to the longest kind in eyebrow caps.

tokens.name: col-matrix-axis
tokens.usage: The risk matrix's axis label column, sized to its longest likelihood band in caption.

tokens.name: col-classification
tokens.usage: The schedule table's classification column, sized to an aligned schedule badge (--badge-aligned-width, the longest word, waiting on deps) plus the why beside it in caption.

tokens.name: col-slug
tokens.usage: The schedule table's work-item slug column, sized to a slug in mono-id without truncating the ones a decomposition writes.

tokens.name: col-request
tokens.usage: The schedule table's request column, sized to a request id or slug in mono-id — the same family as col-slug, one rung narrower because a request key is shorter than a work item's.

tokens.name: col-status
tokens.usage: The schedule table's work-item status column, sized to the longest status word (in progress) plus its glyph in a plain chip.

tokens.name: col-score
tokens.usage: The schedule table's priority column, sized to a score in tabular mono-id.

tokens.name: col-risk
tokens.usage: The schedule table's risk column, sized to the longest risk level in a chip.

tokens.name: col-claim
tokens.usage: The schedule table's claim column, sized to a run id in mono-id.

tokens.name: control-xs
tokens.usage: A segment inside an inline segmented control, where the group is the pointer target and the segment is a division of it. The one control permitted below hit-min, and only inside a group.

tokens.name: control-sm
tokens.usage: Icon buttons, chips with an action, inline selects in a table.

tokens.name: control-sm-5
tokens.usage: The half rung between control-sm and control-md, named the way space-0-5 is: a tool-call row's header, which is taller than an icon button because it holds a line of label, and shorter than a button because it is a row.

tokens.name: control-md
tokens.usage: Default button, input, select.

tokens.name: control-lg
tokens.usage: Gate answer buttons and the command palette input — the controls that carry consequence.

tokens.name: icon-sm
tokens.usage: Status glyph inside a chip, disclosure triangle.

tokens.name: icon-md
tokens.usage: Row icons, node type glyphs, sidebar icons.

tokens.name: sidebar-width
tokens.usage: The primary sidebar, and the Plan request rail beside it. Collapsible to icon-only at 48px, and draggable between pane-min-sidebar and pane-max-sidebar (#276).

tokens.name: sidebar-width-collapsed
tokens.usage: The primary sidebar below the sidebar breakpoint: icon-only, no labels.

tokens.name: panel-width
tokens.usage: The docked right panel that holds artifacts, the Runs step detail and the workflow node inspector: the default width of a side pane. Draggable between pane-min-side and pane-max-side, which are the 320px and 720px this note has always named (#276); a dragged width overrides this token through --pane-<boundary> rather than replacing it.

tokens.name: panel-w-policy
tokens.usage: The permission policy inspector beside the Agents surface's cards (#176). A column of text rather than a pane of chrome, so it is measured in `ch` — a ratio to the type already chosen — and sized to one rule sentence and no wider. Not panel-width: that one is the dock's resizable tenant and this is a fixed column inside a surface.

tokens.name: node-min-width
tokens.usage: The narrowest a workflow or dependency graph node draws, so a graph of one-word nodes still reads as a row of equals rather than of ragged boxes.

tokens.name: node-w
tokens.usage: The width the workflow canvas lays a node out at (#177). node-min-width is the floor a node draws at anywhere; this is the one box a derived layout puts every node in, so a layer reads as a column. A whole number of 16px grid steps, like the three tokens below it.

tokens.name: node-h
tokens.usage: The height the workflow canvas lays a node out at: the kind eyebrow, the name in mono and one line of overlay meta, with the node's own padding around them.

tokens.name: layer-gap
tokens.usage: The gap between two dependency layers on the workflow canvas — the space an edge and its when label are drawn in, so it is the widest of the graph's gaps.

tokens.name: rank-gap
tokens.usage: The gap between two nodes within one layer of the workflow canvas. Half of layer-gap: nodes in a layer are siblings and read as a column, nodes across layers are a sequence and need the room the edge takes.

tokens.name: risk-cell-width
tokens.usage: One cell of the risk matrix. A fixed plot area, not a row: the matrix is read as a shape, so its cells are square-ish at every density.

tokens.name: risk-cell-height
tokens.usage: The height of that same cell, which is not a row height and must not be bound to --row-h.

tokens.name: measure-prose
tokens.usage: Maximum line length for artifact prose and long-form guidance.

tokens.name: titlebar-inset-traffic-lights
tokens.usage: Title bar left padding on macOS, clearing the traffic lights. Zero on Windows and Linux.

tokens.name: titlebar-inset-caption-buttons
tokens.usage: Title bar right padding on Windows, clearing the caption button cluster. Zero on macOS and Linux.

tokens.name: palette-width
tokens.usage: The command palette. Fixed, not a fraction of the window: the list reads the same at 960px and at 2560px.

tokens.name: palette-max-height
tokens.usage: The command palette's result list before it scrolls. Roughly thirteen comfortable rows.

tokens.name: palette-offset-top
tokens.usage: Gap between the top of the window and the command palette, so it sits under the title bar rather than centred.

tokens.name: editor-min-height
tokens.usage: The raw text editor on the Config surface before it is dragged taller: a textarea does not grow to its content the way a pre does, so it needs a floor. Roughly twenty log lines.

tokens.name: splitter-thickness
tokens.usage: The gutter a draggable pane boundary occupies (#276), with the boundary's hairline drawn down the middle of it. Deliberately below hit-min and the one target that is allowed to be: it spans the whole edge of a pane, so it is only narrow on one axis, and every splitter is also a tab stop with arrow keys on it for anyone who cannot land on six pixels.

tokens.name: pane-step
tokens.usage: How far one arrow press moves a pane boundary (#276). The grid step the rest of the layout is built on, so a keyboard resize lands where a dragged one would.

tokens.name: pane-min-sidebar
tokens.usage: The narrowest a dragged sidebar or Plan request rail may become: the nav label and its glyph, with no truncation. Narrower than this is what the collapsed rail below bp-sidebar-collapse is for, and a drag must not arrive there by hand.

tokens.name: pane-max-sidebar
tokens.usage: The widest a dragged sidebar or Plan request rail may become. A rail of nav rows earns no more room than a side pane, and a window between the two breakpoints has to keep a primary pane worth reading.

tokens.name: pane-min-side
tokens.usage: The narrowest a dragged side pane may become — the docked panel, the Runs step detail, the workflow node inspector. The 320px floor panel-width's usage note has always named, now enforced.

tokens.name: pane-max-side
tokens.usage: The widest a dragged side pane may become, the ceiling panel-width's usage note names. Wide output on a 34" display is the reason the drag exists; a pane past this is a person reading in the wrong column.

tokens.name: pane-min-stack
tokens.usage: The shortest either half of a stacked split may become when the boundary between them is dragged — the run tree over the event timeline. Its sticky header and two rows: enough that the pane still says what it is.

z.note: Stacking order for the layers that float over a surface, low to high. A component never writes a bare number (docs/design/RULES.md rule 1); if a new layer needs to sit between two of these, it gets a token here.

tokens.name: z-sticky
tokens.usage: A sticky header inside a scrolling pane, so the rows scroll under it rather than over it. The lowest layer: it floats within its pane, not over the window.

tokens.name: z-menu
tokens.usage: A short list hung off a control — the crumb's counterparts menu. Above a sticky head, below an overlaid panel.

tokens.name: z-panel-overlay
tokens.usage: The docked panel when it floats over the primary pane, below bp-panel-overlay.

tokens.name: z-palette
tokens.usage: The command palette and its scrim. The topmost in-window layer: it opens over everything else, including an overlaid panel.

breakpoint.note: Window-width thresholds for the app shell. A CSS media query cannot read a custom property, so these are not meant to be consumed as var() — build-tokens.js also emits BREAKPOINTS in tokens.ts as plain numbers for matchMedia.

tokens.name: bp-sidebar-collapse
tokens.usage: Below this window width the sidebar collapses to icon-only.

tokens.name: bp-panel-overlay
tokens.usage: Below this window width the docked panel becomes an overlay instead of a grid column.

border.note: Widths and dash patterns; the colours are the border-* and status-* colour tokens.

tokens.name: stroke-hairline
tokens.usage: Every separator and container edge in the system.

tokens.name: stroke-rail
tokens.usage: The left status rail on a run tree row or attention row, and the active-tab underline.

tokens.name: stroke-focus
tokens.usage: The focus ring, drawn with a 1px offset outside the control.

tokens.name: stroke-edge-active
tokens.usage: A workflow graph edge on the executed path; untraversed edges stay at stroke-hairline.

tokens.name: stroke-double
tokens.usage: border-style: double needs three widths to draw — two hairlines and the gap between them — so a subworkflow node's edge is this rather than a hairline. The narrowest width at which a double border is two lines and not a smudge.

tokens.name: stroke-dash-untaken
tokens.usage: stroke-dasharray for a graph edge a run did not take. An even dash: half line, half gap, which reads as the same wire drawn faintly.

tokens.name: stroke-dash-back
tokens.usage: stroke-dasharray for a back edge — the review-to-build loop, a loop body's return. A dot rather than a dash, so rule 4 holds on the canvas: 'not taken' and 'runs backwards' are two different facts and must not be one stroke. Drawn with round caps, which is what makes a 1px-on segment a dot.

tokens.name: stroke-dash-draft
tokens.usage: stroke-dasharray for an edge being drawn in the editor. The longest dash of the three: a draft is a line in progress, not a line drawn faintly.

tokens.name: stroke-dash-soft
tokens.usage: stroke-dasharray for a soft dependency edge on the plan graph (semantics dependencyKind: dashed): preferred ordering that never blocks. A long dash, so it is not mistaken for the dotted informs edge.

tokens.name: stroke-dash-informs
tokens.usage: stroke-dasharray for an informs dependency edge on the plan graph (semantics dependencyKind: dotted): no ordering, only artifacts handed across. Drawn with round caps, which turns the 1px-on segment into a dot.

duration.note: Motion is used for orientation only — disclosure, panel entry, the running pulse. Nothing in this system animates to celebrate. All of it is suppressed under prefers-reduced-motion, where the running state falls back to the animated glyph being replaced by a static one.

tokens.name: duration-instant
tokens.usage: Hover and selection feedback: no transition, so a fast keyboard user never sees a lagging highlight.

tokens.name: duration-fast
tokens.usage: Disclosure open and close, chip state change, tab switch.

tokens.name: duration-medium
tokens.usage: Right panel and command palette entry and exit.

tokens.name: duration-pulse
tokens.usage: One cycle of the running-state pulse on a status dot and of the streaming caret.

easing.note: Two curves. Anything that enters uses ease-entrance; anything that changes in place uses ease-standard.

tokens.name: ease-standard
tokens.usage: In-place changes: disclosure, resize, tab underline.

tokens.name: ease-entrance
tokens.usage: Panels, palette and popovers arriving.

tokens.name: ease-linear
tokens.usage: The running pulse and the indeterminate progress track only.

opacity.note: Three uses, no more. Opacity never carries a status on its own.

tokens.name: opacity-disabled
tokens.usage: A disabled control. Always paired with aria-disabled and an unchanged label colour token beneath.

tokens.name: opacity-stale
tokens.usage: Last-known values while disconnected, applied to the value only and never to its label.

tokens.name: opacity-untaken
tokens.usage: Workflow graph nodes and edges a run did not traverse, in the run-overlay view.
